newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone shuts high street stores to rivals.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone shuts high street stores to rivals.

text.p: Britain's Vodafone Group Plc said on Monday it would no longer sell competitors' mobile telephones in its 300 high street stores.

Unveiling a new corporate structure which brings the Vodafone name into the high street in an effort to boost brand awareness, the group said telephones from Orange, Cellnet and One2One would no longer be available in its shops from Tuesday.

"All retail outlets will sell and advertise Vodafone and Vodafone only," chief executive Chris Gent told a news conference. He noted that people did not expect to go into a Honda car show room and buy a BMW.
Vodafone has been known more as a network operator than a retailer, selling its telephones via six service providers -- Vodac, Talkland, Vodacom, Peoples Phone, Vodacall and Astec.
Talkland, Peoples Phone and Astec are currently selling mobile telephones from all four operators.

Under Vodafone's new plans, which include an updated version of its logo, the six service providers will be reorganised into three divisions, targeting residential, small business and large corporate customers.
